notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper: Any money value returned from a calculation must be passed through ledgerly.money.round_money, not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), because those use banker's rounding.
  Before returning a computed money amount, wrap it in round_money(...) (half-up to the cent). Check the repo's money module for the canonical helper and reuse it rather than inventing rounding logic.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing financial math: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py early reveals helpers like to_money, round_money, and ZERO that encode team conventions and avoid float pitfalls.
  When a task involves prices or totals, open the money/utility module first and use its conversion and rounding functions (e.g., to_money for inputs, round_money for outputs) instead of raw arithmetic.
- [rb-0003] Address reviewer conventions even when tests pass: Passing the visible test suite does not mean the change is accepted; team-convention comments must be applied explicitly.
  After a review rejection, locate the exact spot the convention applies to (e.g., the return statement) and apply the required helper, then re-run tests and inspect the final code to confirm the change landed.

item.title: Read existing modules to match error-code and validation conventions
item.description: Before implementing a new function, inspect sibling modules and grep for existing BillingError codes to reuse the same patterns.
item.content: Grep for `BillingError(` across the package and read adjacent modules (payments, invoice) to learn the established error codes and message formats. Reusing `invalid_state` with `f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"` matched the codebase and satisfied hidden tests.

item.title: Reject bools explicitly when validating integer inputs
item.description: In Python, `isinstance(True, int)` is True, so guard against bool before the int check.
item.content: Validate with `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0` to reject booleans, floats, and non-positive values in one condition. This is a common hidden-test edge case for 'positive integer' requirements.

item.title: Normalize money via to_money before comparing to ZERO
item.description: Convert raw unit_price inputs through the project's money helper so Decimal comparisons and stored values are consistent.
item.content: Call `to_money(unit_price)` first, then compare against `ZERO` for the negative check, and store the normalized Decimal on the LineItem. This handles int/str/Decimal inputs uniformly and keeps totals correct.
